name: dk-uart-rx
experiment:
# Real UART RX test on an nRF52840 DK without changing its flash.
#
# The DK is not reflashed: J-Link memory writes configure UARTE0 on P0.06 (the
# DK's UART TX pin, routed by the on-board J-Link to the virtual COM port) and
# trigger one transmission per STARTTX. The host-side uart plugin must then
# receive real bytes from a real UART. A reset of the target restores it.
#
#   HWLAB_JLINK_EXE=~/sdk/jlink/JLink_Linux_V982_x86_64/JLinkExe \
#     hwlab run --yes examples/dk-uart-rx.yaml
#
# All writes are CONFIRM operations (RAM and peripheral registers only).
name: dk-uart-rx
duration: 22s

devices:
  console:
    plugin: uart
    device: ttyACM0
    baud: 115200
    lines: true
  dbg:
    plugin: jlink
    target: NRF52840_XXAA

steps:
  # message "hwlab uart rx test 01\r\n" in RAM
  - {name: payload, at: 1s, device: dbg, call: MemoryAccess.write, args: {address: "0x20030000", data: "68776c6162207561727420727820746573742030310d0a"}}
  # P0.06 output high (idle level of a UART TX)
  - {name: pin-high, at: 3500ms, device: dbg, call: MemoryAccess.write, args: {address: "0x50000508", data: "40000000"}}
  - {name: pin-output, at: 6s, device: dbg, call: MemoryAccess.write, args: {address: "0x50000518", data: "40000000"}}
  # UARTE0: PSEL.TXD = P0.06
  - {name: psel-txd, at: 8500ms, device: dbg, call: MemoryAccess.write, args: {address: "0x4000250C", data: "06000000"}}
  # BAUDRATE = 115200
  - {name: baud, at: 11s, device: dbg, call: MemoryAccess.write, args: {address: "0x40002524", data: "00e0d701"}}
  # TXD.PTR, TXD.MAXCNT
  - {name: txd-buffer, at: 13500ms, device: dbg, call: MemoryAccess.write, args: {address: "0x40002544", data: "0000032017000000"}}
  # ENABLE = Enabled(8)
  - {name: enable, at: 16s, device: dbg, call: MemoryAccess.write, args: {address: "0x40002500", data: "08000000"}}
  # TASKS_STARTTX
  - {name: starttx, at: 18500ms, device: dbg, call: MemoryAccess.write, args: {address: "0x40002008", data: "01000000"}}

clock.source: host clock at serial read return (rx) / before write call (tx)
clock.note: 115200 8N1 flow=none; rx 23 bytes, tx 0 bytes; the chunk stamp is the first read of the chunk, late by the unmeasured USB and driver latency

clock.source: host clock at RTT telnet receive (target writes are polled by the probe)
clock.note: the stamp is late by the unknown probe polling + USB + TCP latency and never early; lines are not stamped by the target; 3 lines, 112 bytes
